k1p6-14.name: text#14
k1p6-14.text: So far we treated the gradient as already computed. How is it actually computed?

steps.label: KP05 A long bowl needs more than one rate
The long bowl · 1/6
steps.speakerNotes: Back to the toy bowl. Curvature 1 along x and 25 along y: condition number 25.

steps.label: The long bowl · 1/6 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: With a fixed learning rate, x is multiplied by 1 minus eta each step,

steps.label: The long bowl · 1/6 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: and y by 1 minus 25 eta.

steps.label: The long bowl · 1/6 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: condition number \kappa=25

steps.label: The long bowl · 1/6 (4)
steps.speakerNotes: Raise the rate to speed up x and y diverges; lower it to steady y and x hardly moves.

steps.label: The long bowl · 1/6 (5)
steps.speakerNotes: Stability needs a rate below 0.08. Even the best fixed rate 0.0769 only shrinks the error to 0.923 per step.

steps.label: The momentum update · 2/6
steps.speakerNotes: Plain gradient descent only sees the slope now. Momentum remembers where it just went: the update is a fraction of the last update,

steps.label: The momentum update · 2/6 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: plus this step's negative gradient.

steps.label: The momentum update · 2/6 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: Together that is this step's update.

steps.label: The momentum update · 2/6 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: this step's update \Delta w^{(k)}

steps.label: The momentum update · 2/6 (4)
steps.speakerNotes: Then move the parameters by that update, starting with a zero update.

steps.label: The momentum update · 2/6 (5)
steps.speakerNotes: The momentum coefficient is often 0.9; at zero it is exactly plain gradient descent.

steps.label: Two steps · 3/6
steps.speakerNotes: Toy bowl, start 10, 2, learning rate 0.06, momentum 0.8. The first step equals plain gradient descent: 9.4, minus 1.0.

steps.label: Two steps · 3/6 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: Step two: the update is 0.8 times the last one plus this step's negative gradient, minus 1.044, minus 0.9, giving the position 8.356, minus 1.9.

steps.label: Two steps · 3/6 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: Plain gradient descent's second step is 8.836, 0.5.

steps.label: Two steps · 3/6 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: Momentum's loss is not monotone: at step two it is 80.04, above the previous 56.68, while plain gradient descent has 42.16. It rushes with inertia and can overshoot.

steps.label: Two steps · 3/6 (4)
steps.speakerNotes: f(\theta_1)=56.68, f(\theta_2)=80.04: higher than before! (GD: 42.16) step 1 equals plain GD: there is no “last step” yet

steps.label: Cancel and accumulate · 4/6
steps.speakerNotes: Unrolled, the update is an exponentially weighted sum of past gradients, older ones weighing less.

steps.label: Cancel and accumulate · 4/6 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: One result is cancellation: the y gradient alternates in sign and cancels when summed, so the swing shrinks.

steps.label: Cancel and accumulate · 4/6 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: The other is accumulation: the x gradient keeps one sign and builds up; the effective step is the learning rate over 1 minus the coefficient, 5 times at 0.8.

steps.label: Cancel and accumulate · 4/6 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: accumulation the x gradient keeps one sign (flat bowl) summed, they build up: effective step \eta/(1-\alpha)

steps.label: Cancel and accumulate · 4/6 (4)
steps.speakerNotes: Over the same 40 steps momentum is worse at step 2, over 4 times better by step 10 and over 20 times by step 40.

steps.label: Limits · 5/6
steps.speakerNotes: Momentum's loss does not fall every step; it carries inertia and can overshoot.

steps.label: Limits · 5/6 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: The rate still has a ceiling: the stable range is 2 times 1 plus alpha over the largest curvature; at alpha 0.8 the ceiling rises from 0.08 to 0.144.

steps.label: Limits · 5/6 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: So a rate of 0.09 diverges for plain gradient descent but converges with momentum; a rate of 0.2 still diverges.

steps.label: Limits · 5/6 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: Momentum adds a hyperparameter; too large a coefficient overshoots for long. It also does not change that we have gradients only, no curvature.

steps.label: Limits · 5/6 (4)
steps.speakerNotes: too large an \alpha overshoots; it still has gradients only, no curvature momentum relaxes the ceiling but does not make every rate safe

steps.label: Myths and next question · 6/6
steps.speakerNotes: Finally, the common myths and the question left for the next unit.

steps.label: Myths and next question · 6/6 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: “momentum improves every step”. the loss rose at step 2

steps.label: Myths and next question · 6/6 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: “a larger $\alpha$ is always better”. too large overshoots and swings

steps.label: Myths and next question · 6/6 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: “momentum uses second-order information”. it only accumulates past first-order gradients

steps.label: Myths and next question · 6/6 (4)
steps.speakerNotes: So far we treated the gradient as already computed. How is it actually computed?
